ev.q: During 2022–2023, among 28 priority countries experiencing or at high risk for poliovirus transmission, 20 (71.4%) met national AFP surveillance indicator targets
the proportion of AFP cases with adequate specimens increased from 65.9% in 2022 to 79.2% in 2023.
At the national level, the NPAFP rate increased from 3.5 to 5.8 cases per 100,000
The number of VDPV cases decreased from 690 (192 cVDPV type 1 [cVDPV1] and 498 cVDPV type 2 [cVDPV2]) in 2022 to 471
In 2023, 27 (96.4%) of the 28 priority countries** had at least one ES site reporting.
18 (85.7%) met both surveillance indicator targets nationally in 2023, compared with 17 (81%) in 2022.
the proportion of sites meeting the enterovirus sensitivity target increased 41%, from 41.7% to 58.8%.

equity.level_reason: Age <15 years only defines the NPAFP rate denominator; comparisons are across countries, subnational areas, regions and years, which are geography and period, not social position.

level_alternative.reason: A limitation mentions large populations in hard-to-reach areas not accessed by surveillance, which could be read as access raised only as a limitation.

equity.equity_measurement: Units are countries and first-level subnational areas, compared with fixed surveillance targets; no social-position groups.

notes: Table 2 totals are a weighted mean of regional percentages (arithmetic, not survey weighting); 'surveillance sensitivity' is not diagnostic accuracy. The 2022 vs 2023 changes could also justify before/after or trend as a design.
view_issues: Text gives 471 AFR VDPV cases in 2023 (133 cVDPV1, 338 cVDPV2); Table 1 gives 492 (133, 359). The summary's 20 of 28 countries meeting targets does not obviously match the regional counts (18+4 in 2023; 17+5 in 2022).
